1185.overview:
Celtland has been cast into chaos by the theft of Eletale's Book. This mystical volume contains the secrets of the Spirit Tamers. Control Brian, a magician's apprentice, as he explores the expansive countryside and villages on his quest. If he does not reclaim the book, the Kingdom of Celtland will be cast into darkness forever.

The Japanese Version, released a year later (July 9, 1999), contains several Gameplay (Such as the Defense and Agility stats increasing faster) and story differences (most importantly, a different ending). An overview of the changes can be found here (https://www.speedrun.com/quest64/guide/jivof) and here (https://tcrf.net/Quest_64#Regional_Differences).

2922.overview: Heart-pounding gameplay, spectacular graphics and brain-shattering sound effects - guaranteed to have players jumping out of their skins! Incorporates the ferocity of the single-player game with the ultimate bloodlust of the two-player split-screen Deathmatch. A true 3D polygonal environment that includes the most horrific creatures to grace a console. Startling dynamic lighting, levels designed by the masters, and an arsenal of the most awesome weaponry to match.

2924.overview: This version of Quake II differs from the other releases by replacing most of the levels with new ones. Some of the levels have familiar themes or even re-create the original ones closely; however, new stages are dominant, tending to be significantly shorter than those of the PC version. This release also features additional graphical effects, such as lighting during gunfire. Multiplayer for up to four participants is included.

425079.overview:
Quest 64: Hard Mode at it’s core is a difficulty mod of the original story that ended up getting many more changes beyond just difficulty.

A shortlist of most notable features would be

* UI Hud is always visible.
* Stat Growth rates made faster and Stat Caps changed to 999.
* Elements Cap changed to 99, Removed 99 combat level cap.
* All Monster stats are modified (Most cases being 1.5X rounded up).
* Some Monsters were given specific tweaks to make them much harder than the average.
* All “Spirits” are in new locations.
* Some Treasure Chests have had their contents altered.
* Many spells altered, Rebalancing, Deleted, some New Spells entirely.
* Each “Element” is more closely balanced, so that players don’t feel forced to go Earth/Water.
* Item Effects changed.
* 6 New “Items” added.
* Unused BGM’s have been used in certain areas.
* The Start of leaving the Monastery is faster.
* References to “Guilty” in Brannoch removed.
* Optional Area Shamwood locked behind a Key Item.
* Mammon’s World Changed Slightly.

441319.overview:
Quest 64 “French Vanilla” is a quality-of-life overhaul for Quest 64, that came out of game improvements as part of the Quest 64 Randomizer project “MERROW”. Players requested a QoL ruleset separate (but compatible with) the randomizer ruleset. This patch contains only those QoL options. This is not a French translation.

Changes include: 

* Spell damage substantially rebalanced (to make all elements viable).
* Enemy drop limit disabled (enemies will drop items even if you have one).
* Boss spell passive invalidity disabled (in vanilla, some boss spells passively removed buffs, making them functionally useless).
* All spells’ accuracy normalized to 100 (the base game has a flat accuracy check and an Agility vs. Agility check. This functionally removes that first check, but spells can still miss enemies).
* Wings enabled indoors and in dungeons.
* Starting stats slightly improved (50HP/15MP/5Def/5Agi).
* Staff hit MP regain doubled (making Staff-only strats more viable).
* Fast Shamwood (leaving Shamwood will place you back at the Baragoon Ruins exit).
* Dew Drop made useful (now restores 20HP as well as 10MP).
* Hidden spirits moved to clearer locations (three spirits were not visible, now they are).
* Message speed set to maximum by default.
* HUD remains onscreen at all times instead of sliding in and out.
* Minor text improvements added for unclear UI (like ‘Continue Save’).
* Encounter rate reduced.
* Menu now displays combat EXP remaining rather than a percentage.

471754.overview:
After going to the fridge to get a glass of milk, Mario discovers that he's ran out completely. So, Mario goes to the nearest convenience store to get more, but a major accident happens when he tries to get back home...

Help Mario through a short course, as he collects bottles of milk in order to awaken from this coma induced dream world.

479030.overview:
Worlds and memories of the past have collided. Now, a vast interconnected array of lands awaits past the castle doors. Explore, dive deep, and uncover fragments of the past. Along the way, you will be able to gain abilities, both old and new, and recruit more party members to aid in your expedition.

A whopping 250 stars exist within the Creation Nexus. Finding them is a daunting task, indeed... Which is why the sorcerer Omiy is here in castle grounds to help. Once you've collected 50 stars, he will begin to show the names of areas you haven't collected every star in. Rumors say a friendly fey creature will also assist with star detection... But who can say? Regardless, keeping track of which areas lead where is crucial to the exploration of the Creation Nexus... Lest you be lost to time for good.

482881.overview:
Eltale Reborn: Holy Magic Century is a fan-made reimagining of Quest 64. Quest 64 was the first "real" RPG on the Nintendo 64, but a troubled development left it feeling unfinished. A few years later, a Game Boy Color version told the same story with a much fuller narrative. Eltale Reborn takes the GBC game's story and builds it into the N64 game, then expands on nearly every part of it.

Features:

- A rewritten story that follows the GBC version from start to finish, then adds a lot more.
- Towns full of new characters, each with its own little story and side quests.
- Lots of dialogue choices that affect your rewards and how people treat you later on.
- NPCs who remember you, and familiar faces who keep showing up throughout the journey.
- Polish and features from the Japanese release: critical hits, extra effects, menu animations, and map markers.
- A working economy, so you can buy and sell items in town.
- Reworked encounter rates and rewards, so there's no grinding.
- Rebalanced spells for both the player and enemies, so there's no "wrong" build.
- Atmospheric soundscapes for every scene.
